text: At 1550 nm, surface plasmon polaritons propagate only ~50 um on gold (~300 um on silver). Together with the confinement-loss tradeoff, this implies that plasmonics is:
choices: Ideal for long-haul optical fiber links
Completely lossless when silver is used
Able to beat silicon waveguides for meter-scale on-chip routing
Best suited to very short devices where sub-wavelength confinement outweighs the loss, such as 10-20 um slot modulators
explanation: Ohmic metal loss makes long plasmonic paths nonviable, so plasmonics wins only in short structures where extreme confinement pays off, e.g. 10-20 um slot modulators with Vpi*L < 0.01 V*mm. Silver is lower-loss but not lossless, and plasmonics cannot compete for long-haul fiber or meter-scale routing.
